picked.t: The psychological trap behind ‘high salary, house by 25’ social media posts
picked.body: A high school classmate's post lights up the screen: a picture of them gripping the steering wheel of a newly purchased car with a caption boasting their nine-figure income from a side hustle. Scrolling a bit further, she sees a former colleague of her age was just appointed as department head. Anh puts down her phone and stares sleeplessly at the ceiling. The communications specialist in HCMC has a monthly income of VND22 million (US$845), sufficient for a single person, but in the last six months, she has taken on three freelance projects that keeps her working in the evening and both weekend days. Coffee dates with friends have been canceled, and home-cooked meals have been replaced by instant noodles eaten hurriedly at the desk. "I took on extra work not because I was struggling to get by, but because every time I opened social media, I saw peers who had achieved so much in their lives, while I was standing still, and so I was determined to work as hard as I could for a breakthrough," she says. According to the American Psychological Association Dictionary of Psychology, peer pressure occurs when an individual is influenced by members of a social group and changes their attitudes, values, or behaviors to match group norms. Vietnam does not yet have a large body of research on this phenomenon. Nevertheless, keyword search statistics on Google in Vietnam for "What is peer pressure and how to deal with it?" continue to rise. Rather than merely stop with feelings of anxiety, this pressure is turning into risky financial decisions. Quoc Huy, 28, a graphic designer living in Dong Nai, once had savings of VND400 million after 6 years of working. But his life was disrupted when his schoolmates began actively discussing buying land, flipping apartments, and the trend of financial freedom before the age of 30 in group chats. "Going to class reunions and listening to friends talk about billions of dong (VND1 billion = $38,483)made me feel like a complacent and inferior person," he rues. In April 2023, he decided to invest all his savings, borrow VND200 million from relatives, and take out a 20-year mortgage worth VND1.3 billion to buy an apartment in the suburbs. Out of his monthly salary of VND25 million, VND16 million went straight into paying the principal and interest. A photo of the apartment keys posted on his social media page garnered over 500 likes and hundreds of congratulatory comments. But soon after that he had to slash his living expenses to the bare minimum: He canceled his gym membership, declined all wedding invitations, brought cold rice to the office for lunch, and ran the air conditioner for just two hours a night to save electricity. At the beginning of each month, when his phone buzzed with the notification that the mortgage payment went through, Huy would suffer from stomachaches caused by prolonged stress. Vuong Nguyen Toan Thien, medical director of the Lumos Psychological Counseling and Therapy Center, says when one constantly sees others succeed, the person’s brain triggers a social comparison mechanism to locate their own standing. "The brain easily jumps to the conclusion that peers owning a house while you don't means you are a failure." He says when someone is caught in the comparison trap, the boundary between striving for development and a toxic fear of missing out (FOMO) is erased. A person with healthy motivation will head toward goals matching their physical condition and capabilities, but someone trapped in FOMO acts to escape feelings of inferiority, he explains. Borrowing beyond their means and working to the point of exhaustion through the night are actually a compensation mechanism for anxiety, he warns. When prolonged, this stimulates the adrenal glands to continuously secrete cortisol, causing immunodeficiency, sleep disorders, and eroding compassion for one’s self, he says. Thien adds that psychological trauma is even more severe in individuals with those who have faced pressure from family to achieve or have a history of anxiety and depression. Early symptoms include social withdrawal and insomnia, which later progress to panic attacks and chest tightness when presented with information about others' success. To relieve this pressure, psychologists suggest that instead of comparing themselves with others, each person needs to build an emergency reserve fund equivalent to three to six months of basic living expenses before thinking about investing or purchasing large assets. Controlling one’s social media feed by unfollowing or hiding accounts that frequently generate negative emotions is also a necessary step to reduce unconscious comparison stimuli. After a year of struggling under the burden of his mortgage, Huy decided to put the apartment up for sale to clear his debt. He did suffer a loss, but says he has shed the greatest burden of his life. He put the remaining money in a savings account and began renting a room near his workplace for VND3.5 million a month. picked.t: Vietnam among 10 economies set to drive future tourism growth: WEF
picked.body: China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Turkey, Mexico, and Brazil are the 10 largest non-high-income travel and tourism economies by direct travel and tourism GDP, according to the WEF's 2026 Travel & Tourism Development Index. Together, they account for more than 28% of global direct travel and tourism GDP, a share the WEF expects to rise to 35% by 2035. "These economies therefore represent one of the most important sources of future tourism growth." Vietnam's inclusion comes as the Asia-Pacific emerges as the fastest-rising region in the 2026 index. Seven of the 10 most-improved were developing economies in South and Southeast Asia, with Laos, Malaysia, and Thailand topping in that order. Between 2024 and 2026, the 10 economies improved faster than the other 100 in 15 of the index's 17 pillars. The WEF said the group's advantages include stronger price competitiveness, natural and cultural resources, and growing demand for sustainable tourism. The WEF publishes the Travel & Tourism Development Index to assess the factors and policies that enable sustainable and resilient tourism development. The 2026 edition covers the 110 economies across 17 pillars and 102 indicators, including business conditions, safety and security, ICT readiness, transport infrastructure, and tourism services among others.

picked.t: 베트남, ‘국제해양법재판소’ 재판관 첫 배출…동남아 출신 첫 번째 여성
picked.body: 지난 1일 독일 함부르크 국제해양법재판소 취임 선서식에 참석한 응우옌 티 란 안 부교수(왼쪽 두번째)와 신임 재판관들의 모습.(사진=ITLOS) 베트남이 국제해양법재판소(ITLOS) 설립 40여 년 만에 첫 자국 재판관을 배출해 많은 주목을 받고 있다. 베트남 당국에 따르면, 지난 1일 독일 함부르크에 위치한 국제해양법재판소에서는 신임 재판관들의 취임 선서식이 열렸다. 이날 취임 선서식에는 가나와 브라질, 튀니지, 인도 출신 재판관들과 함께 응우옌 티 란 안(Nguyen Thi Lan Anh) 부교수(박사)가 참석해 화제를 모았다. 안 부교수는 국제해양법재판소 설립 40년(1982년), 공식 활동 30년(1996년) 만에 처음 재판관을 맡게 된 베트남 국적자로, 당국은 베트남의 국제 사법기구 참여에 있어 하나의 이정표가 됐다고 평가했다. 앞서 그는 지난 6월 1일 미국 뉴욕에서 열린 제36차 유엔해양법협약(UNCLOS) 당사국회의에서 2026~2035년 임기의 국제해양법재판소 재판관으로 선출됐다. 특히 안 부교수는 1차 투표에서 아시아·태평양 지역 후보 중 최다 득표를 기록하기도 했다. 국제해양법재판소 설립 이후 동남아 출신 여성이 재판관에 오른 것도 이번이 처음이다. 국제해양법재판소는 1996년 공식 활동 시작 이후 총 62명의 재판관(여성 9명)을 선출했다. 안 재판관의 임기는 2026년 10월 1일부터 9년간으로, 그는 독립 판사로서 △1982년 유엔해양법협약(UNCLOS)의 해석과 적용 △분쟁의 평화적 해결 △해양 국제법 질서 강화 등 재판소 업무에 직접 기여할 기회를 갖게 된다. 이에 대해 베트남 당국은 “베트남 최초의 국제해양법재판소 재판관 선출은 베트남 법률 전문가들의 역량과 국제법 준수를 위한 베트남의 기여를 국제사회가 인정한 결과”라고 평가했다. 국제해양법재판소 공정성과 성실성에 대한 평판, 해양법 분야의 전문성을 기준으로 선출된 독립 재판관 21명으로 구성되며, 재판관 선출 과정에서는 세계 주요 법체계의 대표성과 지역적 균형도 함께 고려된다.
